name: Hydrochlorothiazide
route_note: oral tablet or capsule once daily; frequently combined with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or beta-blockers

discovery.by: George de Stevens (Ciba) and Merck chemists
discovery.note: A dihydro derivative of chlorothiazide, the first thiazide, discovered at Merck by Karl Beyer, James Sprague, Frederick Novello and John Baer.

tagline: Thiazide diuretic, one of the most prescribed antihypertensives
summary: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic that blocks sodium chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule. It is one of the most prescribed drugs for hypertension, often in combination pills, and is also used for oedema.
mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide inhibits the sodium–chloride cotransporter (NCC, SLC12A3) in the distal convoluted tubule, increasing excretion of sodium, chloride and water.

The initial volume loss lowers blood pressure; with long-term use, reduced peripheral vascular resistance sustains the effect. Increased distal sodium delivery promotes potassium loss, while calcium reabsorption is increased.
uses: Oedema due to heart failure, cirrhosis or renal disease
Off-label: hypercalciuria and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

history.title: Chlorothiazide
history.detail: Merck introduces chlorothiazide (Diuril), the first thiazide diuretic.

history.title: HCTZ approved
history.detail: Hydrochlorothiazide is introduced by Ciba (Esidrix) and Merck (HydroDIURIL).

history.title: Skin cancer warning
history.detail: The FDA adds information on increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancer to the label, following earlier EMA action in 2018.

history.title: Diuretic Comparison Project
history.detail: A large pragmatic US trial finds no difference in cardiovascular outcomes between hydrochlorothiazide and chlorthalidone.

serious: Non-melanoma skin cancer with long-term use

facts: As a sulfonamide derivative, it can cause photosensitivity and, rarely, choroidal effusion with acute myopia.
